content: Cross-database partial failures require explicit reconciliation: without 2PC, a write can succeed on the source and fail on destination (or vice versa) leaving state split-brained. Standard mitigations are (1) write-ahead/outbox record before attempting remote delivery so the intent survives a crash, (2) idempotent apply on the destination keyed by a stable transfer id, (3) a periodic reconciliation job that detects transfers stuck in an intermediate status and either retries or flags for manual resolution, (4) explicit terminal states (pending/committed/failed) recorded on both sides rather than inferring status from absence of error.
